short: Enhance-then-AV-recognise (M06) is standard: video used twice predates it (2002, 2013); LRS3 0 dB WER 41.1% to 25.5%, but one run, a clean-trained AV baseline and copied baselines.
position: AE-MSR [@xu2020discriminative] changes processing (M06): a lip-guided soft-mask enhancer before an audio-visual EleAtt-GRU recogniser, and a pseudo-3D (P3D) front-end; both are standard. Using the video to enhance and then to recognise was done with HMMs in 2002 and 2013 [@deligne2002avcdcn; @abdelaziz2013twin], and the enhancer is the soft-mask network of [@afouras2018conversation]. The second pass gives large LRS3 gains (0 dB: 41.1% to 25.5% WER, Table 3), but each system runs once, the audio-visual baseline is trained on clean magnitudes (§4.3), and several baseline cells are published values [@afouras2018deep] from more data and other babble. The LRW claim survives the omitted prior results only narrowly (84.8% against 84.07% [@weng2019twostream]), and [concurrent] work reports 85.3% [@martinez2020tcn]. That EleAtt-GRU beats the Transformer is not tested, because front-end, data and decoder change together.
